judgments.question: Give the four Association task strengths, side-I/II task limits, worker requirements when repeating a task before a break, and whether other players workers matter.

requested_parts.requested_part: Task strengths are reputation two, partner three, university four and conservation five
observed_clause_quotes: The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5.

summary_support.quote: - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

- **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.

- **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space and **immediately resolve both its covered-space bonus (if any) and the university tile’s own reputation award (if any)**. You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.

- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

judgments.question: How may a Conservation Project enter play, what are support conditions/once limits, where does its token come from, when is the uncovered bonus taken, and what happens to overflowing projects/tokens?

requested_parts.requested_part: A new project must be played and supported immediately
observed_clause_quotes: Conservation project work can support a project already in play, or play a project from hand and support it immediately; Association II may also play it from the in-range display, paying its folder number, with no refill until turn end.

summary_support.quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

requested_parts.requested_part: New project can come from hand, or in-range display with Association II and folder cost
observed_clause_quotes: Conservation project work can support a project already in play, or play a project from hand and support it immediately; Association II may also play it from the in-range display, paying its folder number, with no refill until turn end.

summary_support.quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

judgments.question: For release projects, must printed standard enclosure size match exactly; what appeal/icons/reputation/conservation are lost or retained, and how do you free enclosure space?

requested_parts.requested_part: Use printed standard-size bands: two-minus accepts one/two, three accepts three, four-plus accepts four/five
observed_clause_quotes: A release project's size category is based on the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5; exact equality is not required within a category.

summary_support.quote: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.

summary_support.quote: - **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.

summary_support.quote: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. judgments.question: Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, do effects count their own card and repeated icons, and which text wins if a card conflicts with a general rule?

requested_parts.requested_part: Upper-right Animal and Sponsor icons count
observed_clause_quotes: Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count.

summary_support.quote: Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

summary_support.quote: 3. **Fill an empty enclosure:** any animal except Petting Zoo animals can go on its own into an empty **standard enclosure** of at least the required size (hexagon number); flip the enclosure to its occupied side. Count distinct adjacent hexes: multiple edges touching the same water hex still count as only one, and a larger water area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. To house an animal in a special enclosure, mark the number of spaces shown on the card with player tokens from your supply; if not enough free spaces remain in the special enclosure, it cannot go there. Special enclosures are never flipped.

requested_parts.requested_part: Additional effects and bonuses follow their respective timing
observed_clause_quotes: On each turn you perform one action using an Action card. Additional effects or bonuses may grant further action resolution as specified by the effect, but the ordinary turn begins with one chosen Action card and its action.

summary_support.quote: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.
**"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

- **Action / Determination:** finish Animals, including moving its card to slot 1, before taking the granted action. Use its Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. A named Action (such as Sponsors) cannot be replaced by taking an X-token; Determination grants any action and may choose the X-token alternative.
